people.title: People from Home Assistant

quiet.title: Quiet hours
quiet.description: During quiet hours, Normal messages wait until morning (they still show on the board). Critical alerts always come through.

outputs.title: Phones, speakers, Glass Message Board and repeats
outputs.description: Critical alerts are read aloud on the speakers and repeat until someone taps "I'm on it". Messages also appear on Glass Message Board as notes tinted by urgency (blue, amber, rose), without a second phone notification.

data.speakers: Speakers that read critical alerts aloud

data.max_repeats: Stop repeating after this many times
data.glass_board: Also post to Glass Message Board (if installed)
data.open_dashboard: Dashboard to open when someone taps a notification

data_description.open_dashboard: Pick the dashboard with your HouseCall card, so a tap lands right next to the I'm on it button. Leave empty to open the app's home screen. You can also type a path, such as /dashboard-housecall/home.

add_person.title: Add a HouseCall-only person
add_person.description:
Create someone just for HouseCall, such as Grandma or the babysitter. They don't need a Home Assistant account and won't appear under Settings → People.

For their phone, pick any notify action they receive messages on. For "home", you can pick a device tracker, sensor or toggle (optional).

edit_person.title: Change or remove a HouseCall-only person

edit_person_details.title: {name}
edit_person_details.description: Change their details, or tick Remove to delete them from HouseCall.

messaging.title: Messaging services
messaging.description:
Reach people outside the Home Assistant app. Tick the services you want to use; anything not ticked is ignored. All of them are free.

After you press Submit, HouseCall walks you through setting up each new service, one page at a time.

Need help? [Step-by-step guide]({help})

data_description.person: Pick someone to choose how each ticked service reaches them. Do this once per person.

messaging_person.title: How to reach {name}
messaging_person.description:
Fill in only what {name} uses. Leave the rest empty.

**Telegram:** {name} opens {bot} in Telegram and taps **Start**. Then close this window, open it again, and pick their name from the list.
**ntfy:** switch on, and the next page shows the channel {name} subscribes to.

Need help? [Guide]({help})

data.chat: Also post their messages in the family channel
data.routes: Other apps already in Home Assistant (advanced)

send_test.title: Send a test message
send_test.description: Sends a short test message now and shows what worked. Nothing is added to the message history.

test_result.title: Test results
test_result.description:
{report}

Press Submit to go back to the settings.

messaging_addresses.title: Where to reach {name}
messaging_addresses.description:
For each app, type how it reaches {name}:
- Signal, SMS: their number with the country code, such as +15551234567
- Email: their email address
- Discord, Slack, Matrix: the channel or room
- Threema: their Threema ID

Leave a box empty if that app already knows who to send to. Separate several with commas.

setup_telegram.title: Set up Telegram (free)
setup_telegram.description:
HouseCall sends Telegram messages through a bot of its own. Making one takes 2 minutes:

1. In Telegram, search for **@BotFather** and open it.
2. Send **/newbot**.
3. Type a name, such as *Our House*, then a username ending in *bot*, such as *OurHouseCallBot*.
4. BotFather replies with a **token** (a long code like `123456:ABC-DEF…`). Copy it and paste it below.

Use a new bot just for HouseCall, not one that Home Assistant's Telegram bot integration already uses.

Need help? [Telegram guide]({help})

setup_ntfy.title: Set up ntfy (free)
setup_ntfy.description:
ntfy needs no account. HouseCall gives each person their own private channel, and they just install the free **ntfy** app.

Keep the server below as **https://ntfy.sh** unless you run your own ntfy server.

Need help? [ntfy guide]({help})

setup_email.title: Set up email (free)
setup_email.description:
HouseCall sends email from an email account you already have.

1. Pick your email provider.
2. Type the email address to send from.
3. Type an **app password** for that account. Gmail, Yahoo and iCloud don't accept your normal password here: create an app password in your account's security settings (the guide shows where).
4. Only for **Other**: fill in the server, port and security from your provider's help pages.

HouseCall checks it can sign in before saving. Nothing is sent yet.

Need help? [Email guide]({help})

setup_chat.title: Set up a Discord or Slack channel (free)
setup_chat.description:
HouseCall can post alerts in a family channel on Discord or Slack.

**Discord:** open the channel's settings (⚙) → **Integrations** → **Webhooks** → **New Webhook** → **Copy Webhook URL**.
**Slack:** create an *Incoming Webhook* for the channel and copy its URL.

Paste the link below. HouseCall posts a short hello in the channel to check it works.

Need help? [Discord and Slack guide]({help})

ntfy_info.title: Last step for {name}: ntfy
ntfy_info.description:
{name} needs to do this once:

1. Install the free **ntfy** app (App Store or Google Play).
2. Tap **+** to subscribe to a topic.
3. Type this topic exactly: **{topic}**
4. If they use a server other than ntfy.sh, tick *Use another server* and type **{server}**.

Or open this link on their phone: {link}

Keep the topic private: anyone who knows it can read the messages. Press Submit to save.

abort.nobody_to_test: There's nobody in HouseCall to send a test to yet. Add people first.
abort.no_services: Tick at least one messaging service first, or connect another messaging app to Home Assistant.

send.name: Send
send.description: Send a message to people. The Hub picks phones, board and speakers based on urgency and quiet hours.

to.name: To
to.description: Who to notify: a name (Jay, Grandma), a person entity (person.jay), a list, or everyone. Leave empty for everyone.

priority.name: How urgent
priority.description: Info = board only. Normal = phones + board (waits during quiet hours). Critical = loud, speakers, repeats until acknowledged.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Mark a critical alert as handled and stop the repeats.

clear_history.name: Clear history
clear_history.description: Remove all messages from the Hub.

send_test.name: Send test message
send_test.description: Send a test message to one person and get back what worked.
